translations.text: There was a man living in Babylon, and his name was Joakim.
He took a wife for himself, and her name was Susanna, the daughter of Hilkiah. She was very beautiful and feared the Lord.
Her parents were righteous before the Lord, and they had taught their daughter according to the law of Moses.
Joakim was very prosperous, and he had a garden next to his house. All the Jews used to gather at his house, because he was more honoured than any of their people.

That year two elders from the community were appointed as judges. The Lord had spoken about such men: "Lawlessness came out of Babylon, from elders who were judges, who were thought to govern his people."
These men were always at the house, and everyone who had a case to be judged came to them there.
At that time, when the people left around midday, Susanna would go down and walk in her husband's garden.
Every day the two elders watched her going down into the garden and walking there, and they desired her, wanting to carry out their own will on her.
Their minds became perverted toward her. They turned their eyes away so that they would not look to heaven, they did not keep to the law, and they did not remember judgement.
Both of them were in love with her, but they did not tell each other about their torment,
because they were ashamed to tell each other about their desires, since they wanted to seize her.
Every moment, all the time, they watched her so that they could see her.
They said to each other, "Let us go home, because it is time for the midday meal." They went out and parted from each other.

But afterwards each of them came back to the same place and met the other. They asked each other why they had returned, and they admitted their desire. Then together they agreed on a time when they might find her alone.

One day, while they were watching, Susanna went into the garden as she had the day before and the day before that, with only two maids. She wanted to bathe in her husband's garden, because it was hot.
No one was there in the garden except the two elders, who were hidden and watching her.
Susanna said to her maids, "Bring me oil and things for washing, and shut the garden gate so that I can bathe."

They did as she had commanded them. They shut the garden gate and went out through the side gate to bring her what she had asked for. They knew nothing about the elders and did not know that they were hidden there.
When the girls had gone out, the two elders got up and ran to her,
and said to her, "Look, the garden gates are shut and no one can see us. We desire you, so consent to us and give in to us."
"If you refuse, we will testify against you that a young man was with you [?] and that this is why you sent your maids away."
Susanna sighed and said, "I am trapped on every side. If I do this, it will mean death for me. If I do not, I cannot escape from your hands.
It is better for me to refuse and fall into your hands than to sin before the Lord."
Then Susanna cried out in a loud voice, and the two elders also shouted against her.
One of them ran and opened the garden gates.
And when this cry was heard in the garden of his house, they rushed in through the side door to see what [?] had happened to her.
And when the elders spoke these words of theirs, her servants were deeply ashamed, for such a thing had never been said about Susanna.
On the next day, when the people came to her husband Joakim, the two elders also came, full of a lawless plan against Susanna to have her put to death. And they said before all the people:
"Send for Susanna, the daughter of Hilkiah [?], who is the wife of Joakim." And they sent for her,
and Susanna came, with her father and mother, her children and all her kindred.
Now Susanna was very refined and beautiful to look at.
The lawless men ordered her veil to be taken off, since she was veiled, so that they might have their fill of her beauty.
But her own family, her kindred and everyone who knew her wept.
The two elders stood up among the people and laid their hands on her head.
But Susanna cried out and wept. She lifted her eyes to heaven, and in her heart she trusted in the Lord.
The elders said: "While we were walking in the garden, just the two of us, this woman came in with two maids. She shut the garden door and sent the maids away.
Then a young man who had been hiding there came to her and lay with her.
We were at the edge of the garden, and when we saw this wickedness we ran toward them,
and we saw them lying together. We could not seize him, because he was stronger than we were. He opened the garden doors and fled.
But we seized her and asked her who the young man was.
She would not tell us. We testify to this now before everyone." The whole assembly believed them, because they were elders of the people and judges, and they condemned her to death.
Then Susanna cried out with a loud voice and said: "O eternal God, who knows what is hidden and knows all things before they come to be,
you know that these men have given false testimony against me. Look, I am about to die, though I have done none of the evil things that these men wickedly charge against me."
And the Lord heard her voice.
As she was being led away to her death, God stirred up the holy spirit in a young boy named Daniel,
and he cried out with a loud voice and said: "I am innocent of this woman's blood."
All the people turned around and said to him: "What is this that you are saying?"
He stood among them and said: "Are you so foolish, sons of Israel? You have not examined the case or clearly found out the truth, and yet you have condemned a daughter of Israel to death.
Go back to the place of judgment, for these men have given false testimony against her."
So the people quickly went back, and the elders said to him: "Come, sit among us and tell us, for God has given you the standing of an elder."
And Daniel said, "Separate them from one another, and I will judge them."
And when they had separated them from one another, he called one of them and said to him, "You who have grown old in evil days, now the sins you committed before have come upon you.
You passed false judgments: you condemned the innocent and let the guilty go free, although the Lord says, 'You shall not kill the innocent and the righteous.'
Now then, if you really saw her, say under which tree you caught them talking together." And he said, "Under a split tree."
Daniel said to him, "You have indeed lied against your own head, for even now the angel of God has received the sentence of judgment [?], and he will split you in two."
And he removed him. And he ordered the other one to be brought, and said to him, "Offspring of Canaan and not of Judah, beauty has led you astray, and lust has perverted your heart.
This is how you used to treat the daughters of Israel, and out of fear they consorted with you. But a daughter of Judah would not put up with your lawlessness.
Now tell me, under which tree did you see them talking together?" And he said, "Under a sawn tree."
Daniel said to him, "You too have indeed lied, for the angel of God is waiting for you with a sword to saw you through the middle, so as to destroy you both."
And all the people cried out with a loud voice, and they blessed God, who saves those who trust in him.
And they rose up against the two elders, because Daniel had convicted them out of their own mouths of being false witnesses. And they did to them the evil that they had planned
to do to their neighbour, as the law of Moses requires. They put them to death, and innocent blood was saved that day.
And Hilkiah and his wife gave thanks to God for their daughter, together with her husband Joakim and all their relatives, because nothing shameful had been found in her.
And from that day on Daniel was held in great honour by the people.
